about: Rename map for the word 'etzhayyim' in awai / itonami / kotoba (owner OK 2026-11-04, JUN-842). Proposal: nothing here is applied. Rules are tried in order; the first whose `match` (case-insensitive regex on one token) hits classifies the token. `status`: keep = never rename; apply = safe to rewrite with the code that uses it (P1); alias = rewrite only with old+new accepted side by side (P2); blocked = needs something first (see `blocker`); lookup = target comes from a table, not a pattern; decide = owner decision per case.

rules.note: A did:web id is bound to its domain; renaming breaks key / signature / record continuity. Keep the old DID; a new DID may be linked with alsoKnownAs. Unanchored on purpose: DIDs also appear inside compound tokens (bond.did:web:...).
Another DID method, also an identity; same reasoning as did-web.
Content / record identifiers (news items, ...): identity-like, referenced by stored data. Keep; add new URNs only if a new namespace is wanted.
Package / repository names ending in the word; follows the repo-path lookup.

rules.blocker: Package names in registries / SBOMs; rename together with the packages.

rules.note: Wire protocol: accept both names for a window, then drop (alias).
Not covered by the awai.network / kotoba-lang.org proposal.
Deployment configuration; renaming breaks running deployments until both are set.
Class / function names: rename with their callers in one change (P1).
Published NSIDs are consumed outside the repos: accept both, emit new.
Per area the owner may prefer app.itonami.* or app.aozora.* (decide per area).
network.awai.* is the reverse of awai.network.

rules.blocker: Contexts are fetched: the new URL must serve the same document (and the old one keep serving) before any switch.
DNS, certificates and hosting for the new names; the old names keep redirecting.

rules.note: Appears as ids, at:// handles and vanity names; depends on the two rules above.

rules.blocker: The @kotoba-lang scope must exist and be owned; published packages need a deprecation notice pointing to the new name.

rules.note: Target is the repository's current home (for example network-awai/actor-X); needs a table, not a pattern.
Drop the prefix together with the code that names the package.
Schema / version identifiers such as etzhayyim.repository/v1.
Fragments of hosts / handles / paths; follows the vanity-url and host decisions.
Prose: reword where awai / itonami / kotoba text names it; leave where it describes the layer above.
